fields.title: Do You Need a Second Region
fields.inputs/0/label: Client requires data storage in a specific country
fields.inputs/1/label: Users in another part of the world complain about loading times
fields.inputs/2/label: We want to survive a data center outage
fields.inputs/3/label: We are afraid a bad release will corrupt data
fields.promptBlocks/0/text: For each situation, state whether multi-region solves the problem and what is cheaper.
fields.promptBlocks/1/items/0: Client requires data storage in a specific country
fields.promptBlocks/1/items/1: Users in another part of the world complain about slow loading
fields.promptBlocks/1/items/2: We want to survive a data center outage
fields.promptBlocks/1/items/3: We are afraid a bad release will corrupt data
fields.referenceReasoningBlocks/0/text: 1 — yes, but as a separate installation, not active-active. 2 — yes, but CDN for static assets and a single region for writes is usually enough. 3 — no, availability zones are enough and are an order of magnitude cheaper. 4 — no, geography does not help at all: you need backups and gradual rollout. Technique: multi-region solves legal and geographic problems, not reliability.
